def: A small module that extends the kit: a coverage adapter lists what the application contains, an authentication adapter recognises a signed-in session.
A capture shown with its numbered markers, its legend and a guided tour, written with a :::screen block.
An inline label of the extended Markdown: a permission, a menu path, a key, a status or a route.
A statement with its Given/When/Then example, defined once with :::rule (a BR-xx id) and cited everywhere it applies, in the business space.
A highlighted box of the extended Markdown (tip, warning, error, permissions, note, recipe, how it works), written as a quote that starts with [!TYPE].
A JavaScript module of captures/plans/ that exports CAPTURES: the pages to open, the actions to play and the zones to number.
A named colour of the site (brand, surface, text…), with one value for the light theme and one for the dark theme.
.doc-kit/context/<page>.md, written by doc-kit context: the only reading an agent needs for one page, instead of the whole code inventory.
The share of the application's routes, registry entries or files that the documentation cites, measured by doc-kit check coverage.
The version of the application the site describes, read in version.file, shown in the site and recorded in every capture.
A build that turns errors into warnings and replaces missing pages and captures with notes (doc-kit build --draft, doc-kit dev).
The comparison of two builds of the same project, before and after a migration, from the HTML bytes to screenshots.
An item read straight from the application's code by doc-kit facts (a dependency, a variable, a route, a table…), written to facts/<source>.json and cited with ::facts.
A page of template feature, written for the business space: one F-xx id, its access box, scenario, business rules and limits.
The file and line of the code that proves a statement, written in backticks: lib/orders.ts:42.
A gap, risk or debt found while documenting, re-checked in the code and numbered by family (C, I, M, P, N).
A route listed in capture.forbidden because its server writes while rendering: the kit never opens it.
An HTML comment left by a page template to say what a section must contain; reported until it is removed.
doc-kit run without a command: it detects where the project stands and offers the next step.
The step-by-step walk through the zones of an annotated screen, one marker at a time.
Either a reading path of the home page (journeys in toc.json), or an end-to-end journey page that follows the product's main action through the code.
The numbered list of a :::screen block: item n explains marker n, so it has exactly one item per zone.
The replacement of sensitive values by dots in the page before a screenshot: GUIDs, local .env values, patterns and masks.
The level a site reaches, from 1 Skeleton to 4 Takeover, measured by doc-kit audit from indicators and thresholds.
One of the 13 page types of the standard, with its sections, its required sections and its word limit.
The capture mode in which every request other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS is aborted in the browser; on whenever a session is used.
A section a typed page must have: a ## heading that starts with its label, checked by the strict build.
The cookies and local storage saved by doc-kit connect after you sign in; a secret that gives access to the application while it is valid.
The part of the documentation written for one audience, declared once in content/toc.json; business and takeover are the two the standard defines.
The file doc-kit build writes for one declared space, with every other space's content physically removed, not merely hidden by the selector.
doc-kit build without --draft: any inconsistency is an error and nothing is written.
A page with "level": 2 in the table of contents, attached to the level-1 page above it in the same group.
sync.json: the hashes doc-kit sync --mark records for each written page, compared later with the application to say exactly what changed.
The section of the site written for the team that takes the project over: architecture, journeys, operations, troubleshooting, findings.
The way a capture plan points at an element of the page: by role, text, field, label, placeholder, CSS selector or block.
The hash of a source file, recorded by doc-kit translate --mark; compared later with the source's current hash to tell a current translation from a stale one.
A statement marked [[verified]] because it was checked directly in the code, as opposed to deduced or unknown.
The .doc-kit/ folder of a project, ignored by git: the session, the zone previews, the audit reports.
An element of a capture that gets a numbered marker; its box is stored in percentages of the image.
